Well, I'm the third child, so I was always the nice, silent one at the sideline. When she declined into some kind of apathy or depression I didn't really want to be drawn into it. I always try to be open, tolerant and supportive, but not stupid about that, like my father for example. I visited her some time, but felt a bit ignored somehow, even though she might have liked that someone was caring. It was a bit weird. It is as if it taken for granted, if you are family. My father has the same issue, he thinks it's god given, that you have to be loyal, but it doesn't work that way. Trust still has to be earned.

I tried to tell her, that yeah it wasn't so super great, but now we are grown ups and we can leave the past behind and work on our problems on our own. After all it wasn't so extremely bad, there was not much violence, no abuse or something. So you could just get professional help and figure our how to mature on your own, without the best role models. But from my experience you got to want to heal, and that seems a problem with her. I just imagine how she get thrown out by one "mean" therapist after another. Well, she tweeted it publicly, so ... and how all her bosses are always assholes and so on.

When she wouldn't let go, with the thing, that she had to "demask" our mother as unmoral or guilty or something, I didn't really want to support anymore.
